blueprint_topic: Management of Care — early individualized follow-up after heart-failure hospitalization
stem: A client is discharged after hospitalization for worsening heart failure. Which follow-up plan best aligns with current AHA/ACC/HFSA transitional-care guidance?

options.A: Plan structured contact within 7 days as a desired goal and choose in-person, video, or telephone follow-up according to the client's risk and available care options.
options.B: Schedule the next routine clinic opening and rely on discharge education unless the client reports new symptoms before that appointment.
options.C: Use an in-person clinic visit as the standard early contact and reserve telephone or video follow-up for clients who cannot attend the clinic.
options.D: Arrange structured contact within 7 days for higher-risk clients and defer early contact for lower-risk clients who have clear discharge instructions.

rationale: A is correct. Section 9.6 of the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline identifies early outpatient follow-up as a central element of transitional care and states that structured contact within 7 days of hospital discharge is a desired goal. The guideline further states that timing and method of delivery—including in-person clinic, video, or telephone contact—should be individualized according to patient risk and available care-delivery options. B is incorrect because it does not preserve the guideline's structured early-contact goal. C is incorrect because the guideline does not make in-person care the default format when other modalities may be appropriate; the method should be individualized. D is incorrect because it converts patient risk into a reason to omit the desired early structured contact rather than using risk to individualize timing and delivery.
educational_objective: After heart-failure hospitalization, plan structured postdischarge contact within 7 days as a desired goal and individualize the timing and modality—such as in-person, video, or telephone—according to client risk and available care-delivery options.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_version_date: Originally published April 1, 2022 with subsequent corrections; current ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub still lists the 2022 guideline, and ACC Clinical Policy in Progress updated June 15, 2026 schedules the Heart Failure guideline update for 2027; sources rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Section 9.6 — Integration of Care: Transitions and Team-Based Approaches, Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 4: early outpatient follow-up is a central element of transitional care; structured contact with the patient within 7 days of hospital discharge is a desired goal; historically this was often in-person, but telemedicine is increasingly used; an initial telephone visit with a nurse or pharmacist may reduce the need for in-person visits when constrained; overall timing and method of delivery (in-person clinic versus virtual visit by video or telephone) should be individualized based on patient risk and available care-delivery options. ACC currentness sources: 2022 HF Guideline Hub; 2026 Clinical Policy in Progress lists HF guideline update for 2027.
source_claim_supported: Current HF transitional-care guidance directly supports a desired structured-contact goal within 7 days after discharge and individualized selection of in-person, video, or telephone delivery based on patient risk and available care options.
blueprint_locator: Appendix A — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Case Management and Continuity of Care: plan individualized care based on need; provide discharge information to home/community; initiate/evaluate/update the plan of care; use referral/transfer documentation; coordinate/manage care; follow up unresolved client-care issues and support continuity across settings.
pdf_visual_verification: Relevant NCSBN 2026 Case Management and Continuity of Care content was visually verified earlier in this 2026-08-20 audit session; no CACHE MISS for the Management of Care locators used here. The HF guideline was verified through the current HTML source; no guideline PDF is relied upon for this item.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'heart failure discharge structured contact within 7 days telephone video in person individualized risk follow-up' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the directly sourced 7-day desired-goal construct while removing all/only and universal 24-hour distractors. The revised options test realistic transitional-care errors involving routine scheduling without structured early contact, defaulting to in-person care, and selectively omitting early contact based on perceived lower risk.

option_audit.A: Correct; preserves the guideline's exact 'within 7 days' desired-goal wording and individualized modality/risk framework.
option_audit.B: Plausible routine-scheduling error; incorrect because it abandons the structured early-contact goal.
option_audit.C: Plausible modality-hierarchy error; incorrect because the guideline directs individualization rather than an in-person default with virtual backup.
option_audit.D: Plausible risk-stratification error; incorrect because risk informs timing/method rather than serving as a reason to omit the desired structured early contact.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable follow-up planning detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel postdischarge follow-up plans.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ACC/HFSA source-based reread.
